site.title: Ícaro, your PDF assistant
site.description: Drop a PDF, ask it questions in plain language and get answers with page citations. Private AI that runs entirely in your browser: the document never goes to the cloud.

hero.title: Ícaro, your PDF assistant
hero.claim: Fly low: your PDF never goes to the cloud.
hero.lead: Drop a PDF, ask in your own words and get answers that cite the pages. Everything happens in your browser: neither the document nor your questions leave your machine.

site.noscript: Ícaro needs JavaScript: the PDF is read and the model runs in your browser. There is no server to send it to.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: Five steps, all on your machine. Vercel only serves static files; there are no functions, keys or costs.

steps.title: Reads the PDF
steps.text: pdf.js extracts the text page by page inside a Web Worker. The file is never sent anywhere.

steps.title: Chunks and indexes it
steps.text: The text is split into chunks of about 350 tokens that never cross a page boundary, and a multilingual embedding model turns each chunk into a vector.

steps.title: Remembers it
steps.text: Chunks and vectors are stored in IndexedDB under the file's hash. Drop the same PDF again and it loads instantly.

steps.title: Finds what matters
steps.text: Your question becomes another vector, compared by cosine similarity: the five closest chunks are the context.

steps.title: Answers with citations
steps.text: A small model answers using only those chunks, streaming token by token, and cites pages like this: [p. 12]. If it isn't in the document, it says so.

models.title: Models and requirements
models.lead: Downloaded from Hugging Face the first time you drop a PDF (not when the page opens) and cached by the browser.
rows: Good Spanish for its size. 4-bit quantized.
Lighter, weaker in Spanish. For low-memory machines.
models.requirements: Recommended: Chrome or Edge with WebGPU and 4 GB of free RAM. Without WebGPU it runs on WebAssembly, but generation is much slower.

items.a: Nothing. Open your browser's Network tab: during the first load you'll see downloads from huggingface.co (the model weights) and after that, no requests at all. The PDF is read in memory and never leaves your machine.

items.q: What gets downloaded and how big is it?
items.a: Two models: one for embeddings (about 120 MB) and one for generation (about 400 MB, or 250 with the fast option). They download once and stay in the browser cache.
Yes, on WebAssembly. Reading and search are just as fast; generating the answer is considerably slower. Firefox and Safari usually fall in this case.

items.q: Does it work with scanned PDFs?
items.a: Not yet. A scan is an image with no text to extract; it would need OCR. It's on the list for a second version.

items.q: How big a PDF can it handle?
items.a: Hundreds of pages, no problem: 300 pages are about 1,500 vectors and search is instant. What takes time is the first indexing, and that depends on your machine.

items.q: Where is everything stored and how do I delete it?
items.a: Models in the browser cache, indexed documents in IndexedDB and chats in localStorage; all on your machine. "Clear everything" wipes it all.
Sometimes. It's a 500-million-parameter model, not a cloud service: it can mix up facts that sit close together in the text. The [p. N] citations are there so you can check.
Icarus flew too close to the sun. This one never goes up to the cloud.

footer.note: No analytics, no cookies, no server. The only downloads are the models, and only when you drop a PDF.
